newsitem.title: UK: LME copper slightly softer, but activity thin.
newsitem.headline: LME copper slightly softer, but activity thin.

text.p: LME copper was slightly weaker in thin pre-market activity as tight dates were about to come into play, traders said.
Three months copper was last indicated at $2,245/50, down from Friday's late finish which took prices up to $2,253/56 from a kerb close of $2,243.
"We saw some modest selling this morning from the Far East, possibly from Japan," one trader said.
The premium of cash over three months metal was a touch firmer around $285/$295 but off Friday's peak of $300/$305, with the tightest dates in late January and early February.
The first tight date is January 29 so the cash-for-a-day could prove interesting in the rings, dealers said.
"There could be some fireworks later on," one said.
The January 29/31 spread is particularly robust.
Cash prices would take the spotlight with three months seen struggling within a $2,220-$2,280 band, dealers added.
Most of the other metals were unchanged to slightly easier along with copper.
Aluminium was last at $1,636, unchanged from Friday's kerb close. Narrower spreads were seen underpinning the market, with cash/threes at $20/$22, little changed from Friday evening.
The market would find difficulty rising to Friday's peak of $1,651, but support should hold around $1,620, analysts said.
Zinc was little changed at $1,137/39 after a kerb close of $1,139. The market was seen consolidating after a blistering rise that peaked last week at $1,157, which was seen as resistance.
The 10-day moving average at $1,128, which was also the low on January 20, was seen as offering support.
Nickel shed $10 to $7,290 and should move sideways between $7,430 and $7,230 near-term. A close above $7,400 would signal a resumption of the uptrend, said chartist Harry Creates of AMT.
Lead was at $701/703 from $699 and may be in danger of slipping further after it violated the $700 level on Friday, dipping to a low of $697, analysts said.
Tin was little moved at $6,000/$6,020 from $6,020, but was showing technical weakness after closing on Friday below the 10-day moving average of $6,026, Broker Brandeis said in a commentary.
Alloy was slightly firmer at $1,530/40 from $1,532/35.
